title: B/C-line refinement for operational hazard instructions (M1: clinician + responder co-set)
context: PLAN v0.2 adds Open Question #8: where exactly does the B/C line fall for operational hazard instructions? The v0.2 default classifies up (e.g. 'evacuate now,' 'is anyone still inside?,' 'do not enter / get out' move to Tier C), but the exact boundary for this class of instructions must be co-set by a clinician and an emergency responder in M1 rubric refinement. The cut is by harm-on-mistranslation, not by topic; a phrase whose misunderstanding could plausibly injure or kill is Tier C even if it reads like an operational instruction. Until this refinement happens in M1, the classify-up default applies. The outcome is an addendum to the criticality rubric (rubric-001 authors the initial rubric; this refines it for the edge-case class). Also establishes the medical-capable-reviewer inheritance for medical/triage Tier-B phrases agreed in the same session.
objective: Convene a clinician and an emergency responder to co-set the exact B/C line for operational hazard instructions and record the agreed rubric addendum.
acceptanceCriteria: A clinician and an emergency responder (not the same person; both qualified in their domain) participate in a documented rubric-refinement session

Session works through candidate phrases (e.g. 'evacuate now,' 'is anyone still inside?,' 'do not enter / get out,' fire-rescue evacuation commands) and classifies each as Tier B or Tier C using the harm-on-mistranslation cut
Produces a written addendum to the criticality rubric (or a revised rubric) recording the agreed classification of each candidate phrase with the rationale
Confirms and records the medical-capable-reviewer requirement for medical/triage Tier-B phrases
Addendum committed as templates/criticality-rubric-bc-addendum.md (or integrated into rubric-001 output) and referenced from the main rubric
Classify-up default applies until this task is complete; M0 packs use the v0.2 default
